core_obligations: Construct an inverse to the restriction map: for a prime of S_0 consider the radical of its extension, which is Z-graded and contracts back to the given prime (proof lines 13636-13647).
Check primality by rescaling a product of homogeneous elements with the invertible homogeneous element, so that the degree-zero part of the product lands in the given prime (proof lines 13640-13645).

Upgrade the bijection to a homeomorphism by showing the image of the graded primes inside a basic open is again open, using the decomposition of the element into homogeneous parts (proof lines 13649-13653).
proof_roadmap: Build an inverse map on primes and verify it is well defined (proof lines 13635-13647).
Compare basic opens to get the homeomorphism statement (proof lines 13649-13654).
difficulty_reason: For a Z-graded ring with a homogeneous invertible element of positive degree, the lemma states that the set of graded primes maps homeomorphically onto the spectrum of the degree-zero part (statement lines 13627-13633). The proof does not cite a general result on group-graded localisations: it builds an inverse by taking, for a prime of the degree-zero part, the radical of its extension, checks primality by rescaling a product of homogeneous elements with powers of the invertible element so that its degree-zero part appears, and then upgrades the bijection to a homeomorphism by computing the image of a basic open through the decomposition of an element into homogeneous parts (proof lines 13635-13654). The rescaling trick is what makes the homogeneous case collapse to the degree-zero case. H2.
